notes: GPT-6 Astra System Card (deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-6-astra), captured 2026-09-22 via headless browser (page is behind a Cloudflare JS challenge; plain curl/WebFetch return 403), converted to text with html2text, change log current through 2026-09-22. This card is safety/preparedness-focused: it contains NO general-capability benchmark tables (no SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, FrontierCode, GDPval, HLE, OSWorld, etc.) -- those live in the separate GPT-6 Astra launch page (performance/openai-gpt-6-astra-launch-2026-09.json). Scored rows here cover: (1) safe-completion/robustness/health/hallucination/alignment/monitorability evaluations for GPT-6 Astra (Sections 4-9), and (2) the same evaluation families for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna via the card's Section 11 appendix. IMPORTANT on Sol/Luna coverage: the safety hub (deploymentsafety.openai.com) listed NO separate GPT-6 Sol or GPT-6 Luna system card as of 2026-09-22 -- /gpt-6-sol and /gpt-6-sol-and-luna both return 'Page not found' (captured: gpt-6-sol.html, gpt-6-sol-and-luna.html). This is NOT an omission: per this card's own 2026-09-22 change-log entry ('We added an Appendix with information about GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna'), Sol and Luna are intentionally folded into THIS card's Section 11 appendix rather than published as standalone cards. Section 11 opens: 'Based on that assessment, we've implemented the same set of safeguards for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna that are detailed in the GPT-5.6 System Card for GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna,' and states Preparedness capability determinations explicitly (High cyber, High bio/chem, below-High self-improvement for both Sol and Luna). All Sol/Luna scores below carry source_id back to this same system card. Many figures throughout the card (most of Section 9 Monitorability, most Preparedness capability figures, several Section 11 Sol/Luna figures) are bar/line charts with no printed axis values in the extracted text; per pack rule 2 ('never invent rates or scores') these are NOT digitized here -- only prose-stated or table-printed numbers are recorded as scores. Chart-only series are listed in missing[]. Where a table used a 0-100 scale (HealthBench length-adjusted scores) rather than 0-1, score is recorded on that native scale with unit 'other' and the scale is noted in caveat.

claims.statement: Per Section 1 Safety Overview: 'GPT-6 Astra is a significant step up in cyber capabilities and meets our Critical threshold. This means that, with the right tools and access, GPT-6 Astra can find previously unknown security flaws and develop new ways to exploit them across many well-protected systems without a person guiding each step.' Also: 'GPT-6 Astra is better aligned than GPT-5.6 Sol... In a simulation using more than 54,000 internal Codex tasks, Astra also received roughly half as many flags for higher-severity misaligned behavior as Sol.' Also: 'GPT-6 Astra's monitorability has decreased relative to GPT-5.6 Sol... In adversarial settings (where we push the model to evade our monitors) we find that the model is able to remain undetected when strategically underperforming in evaluations (sandbagging) and can sometimes evade our internal monitors when asked to perform certain sabotage tasks.'
claims.implication: Astra is OpenAI's first Critical-cyber-capability model under its Preparedness Framework, is measurably better-aligned than GPT-5.6 Sol on offline/deployment-simulation evaluations, but is simultaneously harder to monitor via chain-of-thought under adversarial conditions -- a real, disclosed capability/oversight tradeoff, not a strict improvement.

claims.statement: Per Section 5.2: 'On a benchmark of 1,810 curated attacks from Gray Swan's IPI Arena, Astra's safeguards-enabled checkpoint showed improved robustness relative to GPT-5.6 Sol. The estimated attack success rate across 15 attempts per scenario was 8.5%, compared with 27.0% for GPT-5.6 Sol.' Also, on internal instruction-hierarchy evaluations: 'robustness climbed from 96.23% to 99.79%... Astra has now also saturated robustness at 99.99%.'
claims.implication: Astra is substantially more robust to prompt injection than GPT-5.6 Sol on both an external third-party benchmark (Gray Swan) and OpenAI's internal instruction-hierarchy evaluation.

claims.statement: Per Section 10.1.2: 'Astra represents a significant increase in cybersecurity capabilities compared to GPT-5.6 Sol: it is both significantly more token efficient and more capable at vulnerability identification and exploit development. Based on our evaluations, we believe that Astra meets the Critical cybersecurity threshold.' Also, per Section 10: 'Based on the findings described here, we determined that Astra reaches the Critical level in Cybersecurity capability, and the High level in the Biological and Chemical category. In AI Self-Improvement, Astra does not reach our High threshold.'
claims.implication: GPT-6 Astra is treated as Critical cybersecurity capability (the first OpenAI model to reach this Preparedness Framework tier) and High biological/chemical capability; GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are both treated as High (not Critical) in cyber and bio/chem, and below-High in self-improvement -- the same tier assignments as their GPT-5.6 predecessors (Section 11.8).

claims.statement: Per Section 11.3.1: 'On both the static and multiturn jailbreak evaluations, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna achieve substantially higher defender success rates than GPT-5.6 Sol or GPT-5.5 Thinking.' Per Section 11.2.1.3: 'GPT-6 Sol is generally better than GPT-5.6 Sol at recognizing potential harms in agentic requests and avoiding taking harmful actions.'
claims.implication: Both GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna show broad safety/robustness improvements over their GPT-5.6 namesakes, mirroring (at smaller scale) the Astra-vs-Sol pattern in the main card.
